An automation protocol device id defined how the protocol requires and handles the identification each of the properties, events and commands. Some protocols may have them, others will not. An automation protocol template defines some pre-defined entries of the data of the Driver Definition that can be automatically filled to ease the integrator job with the most common definition or repetitive ones and avoid checking the official documentation every time they are used.

An Automation Task Library is a set of metadata that contains enough information to produce one or multiple Tasks to be used in the Workflow Designer without requiring any code or development skills. Materials are sequenced based on the material priorities with the goal of maximizing the client satisfaction, that is, considering all material priorities and due dates. Forward scheduling is used from the planning start date.
Materials are sequenced using a heuristic with the goal of maximizing the utilization of resources for all materials. Forward scheduling is used from the planning start date.
Materials are sequenced based on the earliest due date with the goal of minimizing the average delay for all materials. Forward scheduling is used from the planning start date.

Materials are sequenced using a heuristic with the goal of minimizing the sum of deviations between the end of the last step and the due date for all materials. Backward scheduling is used based on the due date of each material.
Materials are sequenced using a heuristic with the goal of minimizing the number of delayed materials based on their due dates. Forward scheduling is used from the planning start date.
Materials are sequenced using a heuristic with the goal of minimizing the maximum delay based of the due date of all materials. Forward scheduling is used from the planning start date.
Materials are sequenced based on the earliest due date with the goal of minimizing the average delay for all materials. Forward scheduling is used from the planning start date.
Materials are sequenced using a heuristic with the goal of minimizing the sum of the materials priority weighted cycle time. Forward scheduling is used from the planning start date.
Materials are sequenced using a heuristic with the goal of minimizing the sum of the materials priority weighted delays against the due date. Forward scheduling is used from the planning start date.
Materials are sequenced using a heuristic with the goal of minimizing the sum of the materials quantity weighted cycle time. Forward scheduling is used from the planning start date.

Materials are sequenced in order to minimize the sum of the setup times. Sorting is performed according the setup matrix for the different material products. Forward scheduling is used from the planning start date.
Materials are sequenced using a heuristic with the goal of minimizing the total cycle time. Forward scheduling is used from the planning start date.
Materials are sequenced using a heuristic with the goal of minimizing the sum of waiting times between consecutive steps for each material. Forward scheduling is used from the planning start date.
Sum of Cycle Time for each Material / Total Number of Materials. Material Cycle Time = Time Period between the start of the first Step and the end of the last Step of the Material.
Sum of early days for each Step / Early Materials. Early Days of a Step = Step.EndDateTime – Step.RequestDate.
Sum of late days for each Step / Late Materials.

Sum of Wait Time for each Material / Total Number of Materials. Material Wait Time = Sum of the Wait Times between all its Steps. Step Wait Time = Time Period between the start of a job and the end of its predecessors. Only positive periods are considered, which means overlaps (negative values) are excluded since they aren’t wait times.
Early Materials / Total Number of Materials. An Early Material is a Material that is expected to be completed ahead of the due date.

Total Inactivity Time of all Resources / Total Capacity Time of all Resources. All working periods of a resource that have no job assigned to them are considered inactivity times. Basically it refers to all the periods that a resource could be working, but isn’t.
Sum of all Energy Costs between job Transitions / Total Number of job Transitions.
Late Materials / Total Number of Materials. A Late Material is a Material that has at least one late Step.
Number of late Materials / Total Number of Materials. Late Material = Material.EndDate > Material.DueDate.
Maximum number of early days amongst all the Early Steps. It will refer to the Step that ends the further away (before) from its possible start date.
Maximum number of late days amongst all the Late Steps. It will refer to the Step that ends the further away (after) from its request date.
Sum of the netvalue of all the Materials that finish inside the turnover days period (Material.EndDate <= Scheduler Start Time + turnoverdays)
Total Number of Early Materials. An Early Material is a Material that is expected to be completed ahead of the due date.
Total Number of Late Materials. A Late Material is a Material that has at least one late Step.

Sum of Outsourcing Time / Sum of Time for steps that can be outsourced. Outsourcing Time= Setup + Production Time of jobs assigned to resources of type Outsourcing. Time for steps that can be outsourced = Setup + Production Time of steps that could be executed on at least one resource type Outsourcing.

Sum of Client Satisfaction / (Sum of Priorities * Mean Execution Time). The denominator of the above formula is simply so we can normalize the value (0 to 1). Client Satisfaction = (Material Due Date – Operation End Date) * Priority (Late Operations aren’t considered, client Satisfaction = 0 on those cases).

Sum of Cycle Time for each Material x Priority x Quantity/ Total Number of Materials x Priority x Quantity. Material Cycle Time = Time Period between the start of the first Step and the end of the last Step of the Material.

Sum of late days for each Step Weighted by Priority / Late Materials.
Late Days of an Step Weighted by Priority = (Step.EndDateTime – Material.DueDate) * Normalized Priority.
Sum of Process Time of all scheduled Operations / Total Capacity Time of all resources. For the total capacity time only the work periods will be considered.
Sum of Production Time of all scheduled Operations / Total Capacity Time of all resources. For the total capacity time only the work periods will be considered.

Sum of Cycle Time for each Material x Quantity/ Total Number of Materials x Quantity. Material Cycle Time = Time Period between the start of the first Step and the end of the last Step of the Material.
(Sum of Job Production Times Per Resource * Energy Label Value Per Resource) / Sum of Job Production Times in all Resources
Maximum number of late days amongst all the Late Materials. It will refer to the Material that ends the furthest away (after) from its due date.
Sum of Setup Time of all scheduled Jobs / Total Capacity Time of all resources. For the total capacity time only the work periods will be considered.
Sum of inactivity periods of all resources / Total Capacity Time of all resources.
